title: Police urged to review firearms tactics
article: The RCMP needs to review its tactics when it comes to firing at moving vehicles, a coroner's jury decided Tuesday.
The five-person jury told assistant deputy chief coroner Jeff Dolan that officers need to review the training video, RCMP Dangerous Tactics-Shooting at Vehicles, on a regular basis.
The jury also recommended every police vehicle be equipped with first aid kits and a CPR air mask. The kits and mask must be routinely checked.
Neither constables Tod Abram nor Ralph Overby had air masks in their vehicles when the officers tried reviving Stephen Hanaghan.
Abram shot and killed Hanaghan, 45, on June 27, 2005 when Hanaghan backed a stolen Chevrolet truck into Abram's police SUV.
Hanaghan's sister, Claire Hanaghan, was pleased with the outcome. Although an air mask wouldn't have saved her brother, the device could save someone else.
"They are really valuable recommendations," she said.
RCMP Supt. Jim Begley admitted officers need to check their first- aid equipment on a regularly basis.
"This slipped through the cracks. ... We usually check them every other month or so. Obviously we need to do some (checks) more frequently," he said.
Begley said the Kamloops detachment regularly reviews its firearm training. This includes screening the dangerous tactics video.

Claire Hanaghan did have problems with some evidence police provided during the inquest. Acting as a person-in-standing for the family, she was upset RCMP Const. K.M. McConaghy wasn't present to explain ballistic evidence.

Reading from a written statement provided by McConaghy, coroner's attorney Syd Pilley said Abram fired three shots into the truck driver's door. Abram was standing behind the pickup as it backed into his SUV.
McConaghy didn't explain in his statement why photos of the bullet-riddled door show impact from the front.
Pilley said McConaghy was in Cambodia. He agreed it "would be nice" if he could have attended. This statement brought the dead man's sister to her feet.
"Nice would be an understatement," she said.
Both Pilley and Dolan considered the outburst "inappropriate."
The woman also found discrepancies with Kelowna RCMP Cpl. Sam Ghadban's testimony that Const. Ralph Overby told him he heard Abram's gun go off.
Overby testified Monday he didn't know shots were fired until after he arrived on the scene.
"For me that's a concern," Hanaghan said.
Dolan asked Ghadban if he was concerned about discrepancies in Overby's testimony.
"No. We conducted a thorough investigation," Ghadban said.

Ghadban's testimony included information on a previous incident where Hanaghan and Cikes used a stolen vehicle to ram a police cruiser. The men's fingerprints were found in the vehicle when it was recovered.

Abram was involved in two previous incidents where stolen vehicles tried running him or another officer down. One incident involved shots being fired "in order to protect life." Abram's knee was clipped in another encounter, Ghadban said.
Ghadban was one of 12 major-crime investigators who investigated the shooting.
An inquest is mandatory when a death occurs in police custody. It allows for all evidence relating to a death to be made public.
